content.value_statement: Local roadmaps and ClickUp tasks often drift apart during planning. This skill guides Claude through setup, sync commands, mappings, and conflict rules for ClickUp roadmap synchronization.
actual_capabilities: Explains how local epics map to ClickUp tasks with Epic type.
Documents milestone mapping as ClickUp subtasks under epics.
Lists sync commands for setup, push, pull, full sync, status, link, and unlink workflows.
Describes the local ClickUp sync configuration file and mapping structure.
Defines conflict resolution preferences for status, points, and title fields.
Guides installation of the official ClickUp MCP endpoint for OAuth-based access.
limitations: Requires the ClickUp MCP to be installed and authenticated before live sync can work.
Does not include implementation code for the slash commands shown in the documentation.
Assumes a roadmap structure with epics, milestones, statuses, points, and titles.
Does not define advanced merge rules beyond status, points, and title conflicts.

use_cases.title: Connect Planning to Delivery
use_cases.description: Map local roadmap epics and milestones into ClickUp so product plans stay visible to delivery teams.

use_cases.title: Review Sync State Before Updates
use_cases.description: Use status and dry-run guidance before pushing local changes or pulling remote updates.

use_cases.title: Resolve Roadmap Conflicts
use_cases.description: Apply consistent rules when ClickUp and local roadmap data disagree on status, points, or titles.

prompt_templates.title: Set up ClickUp sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure ClickUp synchronization for my local roadmap. Explain the required workspace, space, folder, and OAuth setup steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new ClickUp integration

prompt_templates.title: Check roadmap mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my roadmap structure and explain how epics, milestones, and statuses should map into ClickUp tasks and subtasks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate mappings before creating or linking tasks

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a safe ClickUp sync workflow for this roadmap. Include pull, dry-run, push, status checks, and conflict handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Run synchronization without overwriting important changes

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose sync conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me investigate ClickUp sync conflicts where local titles and points differ from remote ClickUp statuses. Recommend which source should win for each field.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting after bidirectional sync differences

output_examples.input: How should my epics and milestones sync to ClickUp?
output: Epics should become ClickUp tasks with Epic type.
Milestones should become subtasks under their parent epic.
Planned, in-progress, and done statuses map to To Do, In Progress, and Complete.

output_examples.input: What should I do before pushing roadmap changes?
output: Run a dry-run preview before writing updates.
Check sync status and resolve conflicts before the final push.

output_examples.input: ClickUp and my local roadmap disagree. Which value wins?
output: Use ClickUp for current status because it reflects delivery state.
Use local roadmap values for points and title because they reflect planning intent.

best_practices: Pull from ClickUp before pushing local roadmap updates.
Use dry-run previews before any sync that writes changes.
Check sync status regularly to catch missing links or conflicts early.
anti_patterns: Do not push local changes before reviewing recent ClickUp updates.
Do not authenticate the MCP with a workspace you do not intend to sync.
Do not assume unlinked roadmap items will automatically match the right ClickUp tasks.

faq.question: What does this skill help synchronize?
faq.answer: It helps synchronize local roadmap epics and milestones with ClickUp tasks and subtasks.

faq.question: Does it use the official ClickUp MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs users to add the ClickUp MCP endpoint and authenticate through OAuth.

faq.question: How are local statuses mapped?
faq.answer: Planned maps to To Do, in-progress maps to In Progress, and done maps to Complete.

faq.question: What happens during conflict resolution?
faq.answer: ClickUp wins for status. The local roadmap wins for points and title.

faq.question: Can I preview changes before syncing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends using dry-run previews before writing changes to ClickUp.

faq.question: Does this skill store ClickUp tokens in the roadmap file?
faq.answer: No evidence found in the skill text. The example configuration stores workspace, folder, mapping, and sync metadata.
